content.title: What Is Dyslexia? Signs, Understanding & Support – Dyslexia West Midlands
content.text: What Is Dyslexia? and why understanding it mattersA learning difference, not a limitation. Discover how expert assessment and tailored support can unlock confidence and progress.Why Knowing the Truth About Dyslexia Changes EverythingDyslexia isn’t about low intelligence - it’s a specific learning difficulty affecting how we read, spell, and process words. When undiagnosed, it can lead to frustration, confusion, and missed potential—for both children and adults.At Dyslexia West Midlands, we help you move from uncertainty to clarity with expert assessments, compassionate guidance, and actionable next steps.Dyslexia — Defined ClearlyDyslexia is a specific learning difficulty (SpLD) which primarily affects accurate and fluent word reading and spelling. It exists along a continuum—from mild to more pronounced—and is not an indicator of intelligence.Research shows dyslexia stems from differences in phonological awareness—the brain’s ability to connect letters and sounds—and often co-occurs with challenges like working memory or processing speed. Yet many individuals with dyslexia also demonstrate strengths in areas like reasoning, creativity, and problem-solving.How to Spot Dyslexia in Children and AdultsAges 7-11 years old:Seems bright in some ways but unexpectedly struggles in othersOther members of the family have similar difficultiesHas problems carrying out three instructions in sequenceStruggles to learn sequences such as days of the week or the alphabetIs a slow reader or makes unexpected errors when reading aloudOften reads a word, then fails to recognise it further down the pageStruggles to remember what has been readPuts letters and numbers the wrong way: for example, 15 for 51, b for d or “was” for “saw”Has poor handwriting and/or struggles to hold the pen/pencil correctly and/or learn cursive writingSpells a word several different waysAppears to have poor concentrationStruggles with mental arithmetic or learning times tablesSeems to struggle with maths and/or understanding the terminology in maths: for example, knowing when to add, subtract or multiplyHas difficulties understanding time and tenseConfuses left and rightCan answer questions orally but has difficulties writing the answer downHas trouble learning nursery rhymes or songsStruggles with phonics and learning the letter-to-sound rulesSeems to get frustrated or suffers unduly with stress and/or low self-esteemStruggles to copy information down when reading from the boardNeeds an unexpected amount of support with homework and struggles to get it done on timeIs excessively tired after a day at schoolAges 12 to adult:Many older children and adults will remember having similar difficulties to those listed on the previous page. Some may still apply, whilst additional issues for older children through to adulthood might include:Difficulties taking notes, planning and writing essays, letters or reportsStruggles with reading and understanding new terminologyQuality of work is erraticDifficulties revising for examinationsStruggles to communicate knowledge and understanding in examsFeels that the effort put in does not reflect performance or resultsForgets names and factual information, even when familiarStruggles to remember things such as a personal PIN or telephone numberStruggles to meet deadlinesStruggles with personal organisation (finances/household, arrives at lessons with the wrong books, forgets appointments)Difficulties filling in forms or writing chequesOnly reads when necessary and never for pleasureDevelops work avoidance tactics to disguise difficulties and/or worries about being promoted/taking professional qualificationsDifficulties become exacerbated when under pressure of time.If these challenges feel familiar, you’re not alone, and there are practical ways forward.From Assessment to Action: Your Path to Understanding and SupportDyslexia West Midlands goes beyond a label—we focus on discovery and transformation:Expert Assessment: Diagnostic evaluations by specialist dyslexia teachers or HCPC-registered educational psychologists to pinpoint strengths, challenges, and co-occurring patterns.Clear, Practical Reports: All assessments come with a tailored report containing strategies you can use immediately—in school, at home, or work.Support & Tuition: From multi-sensory literacy tuition to exam access plans (e.g., Form 8) and workplace adjustments, we provide ongoing guidance every step of the way.Why Trust Dyslexia West Midlands?A dedicated team of specialist teachers and educational psychologists—with APC qualifications—offering the depth of a full team, not just one person.Informed by real experience—working with schools, parents and neurodiverse learners across the West Midlands.Flexible access: in-person in Coventry or remotely from the comfort of your home.Compassionate, no-cost 20-minute consultations—supporting you to explore
